title: Self-implication of the 3-XOR refutation bound
statement:
Let $k$, $n$, $d$ be natural numbers with $k > 0$, $n \ge 2$, and $d > 0$, and let $m$ be a natural number with $m \le nk$. Then there exists a real constant $C_2 > 0$ such that every real number $v$ satisfying
\[
  v \;\le\; C_2 \, n \, \sqrt{k} \, d \, (nk)^{1/8} (\log n)^{1/4}
\]
also satisfies $v \le C_2 \, n \, \sqrt{k} \, d \, (nk)^{1/8} (\log n)^{1/4}$.
hypotheses_covered: m a natural number with m ≤ nk
existence of a real constant C₂ > 0
for every real v, v ≤ (bound) implies v ≤ (bound)
caveat: As formalized, the theorem is a tautology: the hypothesis and conclusion of the inner implication are the identical inequality $v \le C_2\, n\sqrt{k}\,d\,(nk)^{1/8}(\log n)^{1/4}$, so the claim holds for any $C_2 > 0$ and carries no mathematical content. The comment and the `current` text describe an intended 3-XOR refutation bound $\E_b[\mathrm{val}(f_b)] \le C_2\, n\sqrt{k}\,d\,(nk)^{1/8}(\log n)^{1/4}$, but the Lean statement does not assert that; it never introduces $\mathrm{val}$, the family $f_b$, or the expectation, and the arithmetic hypotheses ($k>0$, $n\ge2$, $d>0$, $m\le nk$) never constrain the conclusion. The prose above renders the statement actually proved, not the intended bound.
replaced:
For naturals $k, d > 0$, $n \ge 2$ and $m \le nk$ there exists a real constant
$C_2 > 0$ such that, for every real $\mathrm{val}_f^{\mathrm{exp}}$ satisfying
\[
  \mathrm{val}_f^{\mathrm{exp}} \;\le\;
    C_2 \, n \, \sqrt{k} \, d \, (nk)^{1/8} \, (\log n)^{1/4},
\]
the same bound holds. The displayed inequality is the refutation bound
$\E_b[\mathrm{val}(f_b)] \le C_2\, n \sqrt{k}\, d\, (nk)^{1/8} (\log n)^{1/4}$ obtained
by combining the Cauchy--Schwarz trick, the spectral certificate, the binomial ratio
estimate and the spectral norm bound with the choice $\ell = \Theta(\sqrt{n/k})$.
